title: Applied ML Eval Harness Standards and Integrated Playbooks
author: Ava Patel
body:
Summary

This doc collects our standards, checklists, and runbooks for the Applied ML eval harness and surrounding operational playbooks. It is intended as the single-source reference for: (1) eval-harness architecture and onboarding; (2) prompt-set and benchmark cataloging; (3) model onboarding checklist; (4) quality guardrails and alerting thresholds; (5) quantization profile guidance; and (6) regression detection and triage.

Scope

- Audience: ML Engineers, Applied ML, Model Ops, Platform Engineers, and SREs.
- Coverage: Hosted/Dedicated/Private model variants used for inference on Redwood.
- Not covered: research-only experiments that are not intended for serving. Those should live in the research wiki.

Ownership and Roles

- Eval harness owner: Applied ML (primary) — Diego Martinez
- Platform integrations & infra support: Eng Infra — Li Wei
- Quality triage & on-call: Eng SRE — Sophia Reynolds
- Model owner: team that owns the feature/serving route (must be listed on model metadata)

Design Principles

1) Production-first: all evals used for rollouts must be reproducible, versioned, and runnable in CI.
2) Lightweight & extensible: the harness must support new metrics and prompt formats without build changes.
3) Guardrails over perfection: automated checks should prevent the most common regressions (hallucination, latency spikes, embedding drift).
4) Signal hierarchy: automated alerts -> triage checklist -> human review -> rollback/canary changes.

1) Eval Harness: Architecture & Standards

Intro
The eval-harness is a service-backed framework (service name: eval-harness-service) that runs deterministic prompt sets, collects model outputs, computes metrics, and stores results in the evaluation store (postgres + S3 artifact bucket). The harness exposes a reproducible CLI and a job spec for CI and batch jobs.

Key components
- Runner: executes prompt batches against a target model variant (supports streaming and non-streaming calls).
- Metric library: vectorized, versioned metrics (accuracy, exact match, ROUGE, BLEU, embedding-similarity, hallucination-rate).
- Orchestration: Kubernetes-backed job controller (k8s-job-runner) with resource classes for gpu/cpu.
- Storage: evaluation DB (Postgres) + artifacts (S3) + provenance metadata in model-catalog.
- API: internal REST for scheduling and retrieving runs (auth via service tokens).

Minimum requirements for an eval run
- Run spec must include: model_variant_id, prompt_set_id, seed, batch_size, max_tokens, sampling_params (top_k/top_p/temperature).
- All runs must be tagged with git_sha and harness_version.
- Results must include per-example outputs, token-level latencies, and metric breakdowns.

CI integration
1. New model pull requests must include a smoke eval that runs 100 representative prompts (fast tests).
2. Pre-release flows (canary/blue-green) must run full prompt sets (see Prompt Sets section).
3. Test artifacts must be uploaded to S3 with lifecycle tag: eval-artifacts/<model_variant>/<date>/run-id.json

2) Prompt Sets & Benchmarks

Cataloging rules
- Prompt sets must be added to the prompt catalog with metadata: author, domain, dataset_size, seed, label_schema, supported_metrics, and intended_use (smoke|canary|release).
- Prompts are versioned semantically (v1.0.0) and pinned in eval run specs.

Prompt types and example usage
- Smoke sets: 50-200 examples focused on critical flows (auth, summarization, safety). Used in PRs.
- Canary sets: 500-2,000 examples representing production traffic sampling. Used in canary rollouts.
- Release/regression suites: 2k-20k examples, stratified by customer-facing buckets and adversarial sets.

Benchmark metrics (standardized)
- Utility: exact_match (EM), F1, BLEU, ROUGE-L, BLEU-4 (as applicable).
- Robustness & safety: hallucination_rate, toxicity_score (from safety model), refusal_rate.
- Efficiency: median_latency_ms, p95_latency_ms, tokens_per_second, cost_per_1k_tokens_estimate.
- Retrieval/semantic: embedding_cosine_mean, retrieval_precision@k.

Prompt-set labeling and ownership
- Every prompt set must have an owner (team) and a review cadence (quarterly).
- Sensitive customer prompts must be stored under restricted confidentiality and excluded from public datasets.

3) Model Onboarding Guide (Checklist)

Add model_variant to model-catalog with the following steps:

Pre-onboarding
1. Register model in model-catalog: model_id, variant_id, architecture, size, quantization_profile (if any), owner, contact.
2. Provide model card: capabilities, limitations, known failure modes, recommended sampling defaults.

Onboarding steps (minimum gated checks)
1. Smoke eval: run smoke prompt set (owner verifies no critical correctness regressions).
2. Latency & cost profiling: measure median/p95 latency on representative sequences (1, 32, 512 tokens) and estimate per-token cost.
3. Safety scan: run safety classifier and adversarial prompt suite. Threshold: toxicity_score < 0.02 average on high-risk prompts.
4. QA sign-off: applied-ml or product owner must approve results and create release notes.
5. Canary rollout: deploy to <= 5% of traffic with guardrail monitoring enabled. If any metric breach occurs, auto-roll back.

Required artifacts
- eval run_id UUID for full-release eval (link to S3 artifact).
- perf profile CSV (tokens, latency_ms, GPU_util).
- quantization compatibility report (if quantized).

4) Quality Guardrails and Monitoring

Guardrail categories
- Correctness regressions: EM/F1 drops > 3% relative to baseline (or absolute depending on metric).
- Safety regressions: increase in hallucination_rate > 2% absolute or toxicity_score delta > 0.01.
- Performance regressions: p95 latency > 1.5x baseline or error rate > 0.5%.

Example alert thresholds (configurable per model)
| metric | baseline | alert threshold | severity |
|--------|----------|-----------------|----------|
| p95_latency_ms | 420 | > 630 | P1 |
| hallucination_rate | 0.03 | > 0.05 | P1 |
| exact_match | 0.78 | < 0.75 | P2 |
| refusal_rate | 0.01 | > 0.03 | P2 |

Monitoring signals and dashboards
- Dashboards: per-model route: latency, token throughput, error rate, key eval metrics, recent eval run links.
- Alerts: pushed to PagerDuty (severity mapping above) with run_id and link to failing examples.
- Canary auto-rollback policy: if any P1 alert fires during canary, k8s deployment is immediately rolled back and traffic shifted to previous variant.

5) Quantization Profiles and Compatibility

Purpose
- Provide tested quantization configurations that balance performance and quality across common architectures (transformer decoder-only, encoder-decoder).

Profiles (examples)
- fq8-fast: 8-bit float-like quantization optimized for latency-sensitive routes. Expect 5-8% quality delta on sensitive NLP tasks; recommended for non-critical UIs.
- int4-eff: 4-bit integer profile for cost-sensitive batch workloads. Expect 8-15% quality delta; only allowed for background or low-SLA embedding jobs.
- hybrid-qa: per-layer mixed precision that keeps attention/softmax in fp16 and quantizes MLP to int8; best for question-answering workloads.

Compatibility table
| model_family | recommended_profile | expected_quality_delta | allowed_for | owner_approval_required |
|--------------|---------------------|------------------------|-------------|-------------------------|
| redwood-1-small | fq8-fast | ~5% | hosted dev | no |
| redwood-1-xxl | hybrid-qa | ~2% | dedicated/canary | yes |
| community-llama-2 | int4-eff | ~10% | private batch | yes |

Quantization validation checklist
1. Run full regression suite against float32 baseline.
2. Verify top-k and sampling behavior with 100 deterministic seeds.
3. Evaluate hallucination and safety prompt sets; ensure no >2% absolute increase in hallucination_rate.
4. Produce quantization report that lists per-layer changes and a recommendation flag (accept/reject/manual review).

6) Regression Triage Playbook

Detection flow
1. Automated runs and production telemetry detect a regression (alert fires with run_id and example subset).
2. PagerDuty/on-call notified with links to failing examples and recent deploys.

Immediate triage (first 30 minutes)
1. Acknowledge incident and collect context: model_variant, deploy time, recent config changes (sampling params, quantization), infra events.
2. Reproduce failure locally using the eval-harness with the run_id and seed.
3. If reproducible and severity P1 — trigger emergency rollback to previous variant and notify stakeholders.

Post-rollback analysis (2-72 hours)
1. Triage owner (model owner + applied-ml) runs targeted A/B tests isolating variables (quantization on/off, sampling param diffs, model weights).
2. Create a regression ticket with: hypothesis, repro steps, failing examples, metric deltas, and remediation plan.
3. If root cause is infra (hardware, kernel patch), engage Eng Infra and SRE. If model-related, engage research/modeling.

Priority and SLAs
- P1 regressions: engage within 15 minutes, rollback if needed, full postmortem draft within 72 hours.
- P2 regressions: engage within 2 business hours, fix/mitigation within sprint cadence.

Communication and runbooks
- All regression incidents must have a running timeline in the incident doc and linked postmortem.
- Playbook owners must maintain a regression checklist and runbook in the applied-ml directory.

7) Runbooks, Tools, and Common Commands

Common CLI commands
- Run harness smoke test: evalctl run --model <variant> --prompt-set smoke-<domain> --size 100 --out s3://eval-artifacts/<model>/smoke-run.json
- Reproduce artifact: evalctl reproduce --run-id <uuid> --local
- Canary deploy (k8s): kubectl apply -f canary-deployment.yaml --context=redwood-prod && rollouts set image <route> <variant>

Useful dashboards
- /dashboards/eval/summary: per-model summary of latest runs and metric trends.
- /dashboards/canary/health: canary health over last 24h with per-route breakdown.

Appendix: Example Eval Run Spec (YAML)
```yaml
run_spec:
  model_variant_id: "rw-1.2.0-quant-hybrid-2029-03"
  prompt_set_id: "canary-summarization-v2"
  seed: 42
  batch_size: 16
  max_tokens: 256
  sampling_params:
    temperature: 0.0
    top_k: 50
    top_p: 0.95
  harness_version: "2.4.1"
  git_sha: "a1b2c3d4"
  tags: ["canary","summary","quarters-2029-Q1"]
```

Maintenance and Review Cadence
- This doc and the prompt catalog must be reviewed quarterly by Applied ML leads.
- Quantization profiles require validation for each new major model family and a security review for any restricted deployment.
